searchText: This was recently ddscussed elsewhere (I don't remember where) in this server. On a related note: I feel like binding development to named forks is going to result in a *lot* of pain and I recommend not doing that. It is incredibly common in the EL world for features to be coded in clients long prior to them finalizing into a fork, and some changesets live in clients for many forks before finally getting activated in a hardfork. in many ways, I think it would be clearer / more clean to _not_ merge any eip4844 work at all and keep it in a rebased feature branch until capella is shipped - then we have a go/no-go for 4844 in the next HF and _that's_ when everything is merged That’s one option, but it would be hard to progress the api if I block them on the data types… I’d prefer that to not be the thing that stops 4844 being ready why? I mean, if everything is neatly merged to a 4844 feature branch that periodically gets rebased, the data types would also be in that branch? Beacon-apis is trunk development But true, might be worth it being on a branch
